skill.name: decision-records
skill.description: Create, validate, promote, archive, rename, and supersede ADR-style decision records with generated indexes and cross-links.
skill.summary: Manage decision records and keep their lifecycle, index, and links consistent.
skill.author: skymavis

security_audit.summary: All 288 static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, draft mnemonics, relative links, placeholder URLs, or argument-array Git subprocesses. Manual review found a high-severity persistent agent-instruction pattern and a medium-severity installer overwrite risk.

remediation.issue: The scaffolded AGENTS.md claims that the skill overrides conflicting repository instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Remove priority claims and limit guidance to decision-record files. Never instruct agents that skill content outranks repository, user, or platform instructions.

remediation.issue: Install removes an existing scripts/decisions.py without confirmation or backup.
remediation.suggestion: Refuse installation when a non-managed destination exists. Require explicit replacement approval or preserve the existing file before creating the symlink.

content.value_statement: Decision records become stale when identifiers, links, and lifecycle states drift. This skill manages drafts, promotions, indexes, validation, and cross-references.
actual_capabilities: Scaffold decision directories, templates, repository entry points, and a pre-commit validation hook.
Generate an index for accepted, superseded, and deprecated decision records.
Validate front matter, identifiers, counters, statuses, references, links, and generated index freshness.
Promote approved drafts into numbered records while updating headings, references, paths, and lifecycle fields.
Rename draft identifiers and update matching references across Markdown documentation.
Warn about identifier collisions with a locally available origin/main reference without fetching the network.
limitations: Promotion and supersession require explicit human approval because they finalize records and move files.
Automatic reference rewriting is limited to Markdown files under the documentation tree.
Remote collision checks use only the local origin/main reference and never fetch updates.
Installation modifies repository files, creates a symlink, and may add a pre-commit hook.

use_cases.title: Capture Architecture Decisions
use_cases.description: Create structured drafts for technical choices, alternatives, consequences, and related records.

use_cases.title: Maintain Governance Records
use_cases.description: Track policy, legal, security, or operational decisions through accepted and retired states.

use_cases.title: Validate Documentation in CI
use_cases.description: Detect stale indexes, broken links, invalid metadata, duplicate identifiers, and lifecycle inconsistencies before merge.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Decision Draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a decision draft about [topic]. Include context, the proposed decision, rationale, alternatives, consequences, risks, and relevant record references.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin a new decision record from a clear topic.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Review draft [ID] for complete front matter, clear rationale, realistic alternatives, consequences, unresolved risks, and valid decision references. Suggest focused edits.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare an existing draft for team review.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an Approved Promotion
prompt_templates.prompt: I approve promoting draft [ID]. Check dependencies and replacement effects, show the planned changes, then promote it and validate the decision registry.
prompt_templates.scenario: Finalize a reviewed draft with explicit approval.

prompt_templates.title: Supersede a Decision Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a replacement for decision [ID] using these changes: [changes]. Map affected references, explain consequences, and wait for approval before promotion.
prompt_templates.scenario: Replace an accepted decision while preserving history and links.

output_examples.input: Draft a decision to standardize PostgreSQL for transactional services.
output_examples.output: A draft decision with context, PostgreSQL as the proposed choice, evaluated alternatives, consequences, risks, and a four-letter draft identifier.

output_examples.input: Check the decision registry before merge.
output_examples.output: A concise validation result listing stale indexes, invalid metadata, broken references, or a successful check when no issues remain.
A numbered accepted record, refreshed inbound links, an updated index, and a final validation result after explicit approval.

best_practices: Keep each record focused on one decision with explicit context, alternatives, consequences, and deciders.
Reference records by identifier and regenerate links and the index after lifecycle changes.
Review promotion plans and obtain explicit approval before accepting or superseding records.
anti_patterns: Do not edit generated indexes or generated record links by hand.
Do not rewrite an accepted decision to change direction; create a superseding record.
Do not promote drafts with unresolved references, incomplete metadata, or missing human approval.

faq.question: What record types are supported?
faq.answer: Any lowercase type slug is supported, including architecture, product, security, policy, legal, finance, and operations.

faq.question: Does the skill fetch origin/main?
faq.answer: No. It reads the local reference when available and remains silent when that reference is absent.

faq.question: Can it promote a draft automatically?
faq.answer: No. Promotion requires explicit human approval in the current interaction because it finalizes and moves the record.

faq.question: How are accepted decisions changed?
faq.answer: Minor approved maintenance is allowed. Direction changes require a new record that supersedes the accepted decision.

faq.question: Which files can reference decisions?
faq.answer: Markdown files under the documentation tree can reference decision identifiers and receive generated relative links.

faq.question: What does installation change?
faq.answer: It creates documentation scaffolding, links the tool into scripts, updates gitignore, creates missing entry points, and may add a pre-commit hook.
